LESSON: ADDITION (8

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.2: Addition (8

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Addition (8. Read, look at the pictures, practise, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: LEARN

Welcome to a mathematics program for grade four. today, we are going to learn about addition of capacity in litres. this lesson, we will require the following, Two five litre containers, Water, a bucket. A Basin. A large container. A pen or a pencil and a notebook. Welcome to Mathematic for Grade four. In our last lesson we learnt about use of half and quarter litre containers to measure capacity. Today, we shall go ahead and do additions of capacity in litres. In grade three, we learned about adding capacity in litres and in this lesson we shall do the same. Learner, fill the two five litre containers with water. fill the two five litre containers with water. Pour the water from the two five litre container into a larger container. Pour water from the two five litre containers into a larger container. Use a one litre container to measure how much water is in the larger container, use a one litre container to measure how much water is in the larger container. Confirm by adding five to five as the total amount of water in the container. Confirm by adding five to five as the total amount of water in that container. Good attempt if you have 10 litres as your answer, then you are correct. Yes, our larger container has a capacity of 10 litres. Learner, it's important to remember the addition methods we learnt in our lower grades on regrouping. Yes, it is important to remember the addition methods we learnt in our lower grades on regrouping. Now, Learner, listen attentively to the number story below. Mzee Matope’s cows produce one hundred and fifty four litres of milk in the morning. And one hundred and sixty three litres in the evening. How many litres of milk do the cows produce in a day? I will repeat. Mzee Matope’s cows produce one hundred and fifty four litres of milk in the morning. And one hundred and sixty three litres in the evening. How many litres of milk do the cows produce in a day? In the number story read, We have to add one hundred and fifty four litres of milk produced in the morning to one hundred and sixty three litres of milk produced in the evening. To do addition, we start by looking at the ones and add four to three, which gives us seven. Write Seven in ones place value.

Add Tens, that is five and six, which gives us 11. Write One in tens place value and regroup one in hundreds place. Add hundreds. That is one plus one plus the regroup one, which makes three hundred and write three in hundreds place value. The total capacity of milk produced in a day by Mzee Matope’s cows is three hundred and seventeen litres. Yes, Mzee Matope’s cows produce three hundred and litres of milk every day, if you are able to get three hundred and seventy litres as your answer, then Goodbye. Your radio teacher was Scholah Mkandoh. The program was written and produced by the It was recorded by John Mbithi for the Institute of Curriculum Development. Until next time. Goodbye.

SECTION 3: TRY THIS

1. Look again at the examples or pictures above.
2. Tell a parent or friend what Addition (8 means, using your own words.
3. Copy one example into your exercise book and change it to fit your school or home.
4. Underline three new words and find out what they mean.

SECTION 4: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Addition (8.
2. Complete any “Work to do” items shown in the pupil book pages above.
3. Create three of your own practice questions on this topic.
4. Answer the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after finishing.

SECTION 5: REMEMBER

1. Topic: Addition (8
2. Subject: MATHEMATICS
3. Learning materials: Maths Prg 6 addition of capacity 
4. Revise with the quiz now.
